_note: Simulated news events. Fictional and clearly labelled; they give agents something to react to. The set is balanced: proposals that lean economically left and right, and socially toward more freedom and more control, so the measurement is not pushed one way by the inputs.

events.title: Simulated news: Finance ministry floats a 2% annual wealth tax on fortunes above 50 crore
events.body: The proposal would fund rural health and schools. Industry groups warn of capital flight; supporters call it overdue. Comments are open.

events.title: Simulated news: State proposes reserving 70% of private sector jobs for locals
events.body: Companies with more than 50 employees would have to hire Karnataka residents for most roles. Tech firms say they may expand elsewhere.

events.title: Simulated news: Draft rule would require government ID to open any social media account
events.body: Officials say it will curb fake accounts and hate speech. Digital rights groups say it ends anonymous speech.

events.title: Simulated news: City plans to privatise loss-making BEST bus routes
events.body: Private operators would run 40% of routes under contract. Unions announce protests over job security and fares.

events.title: Simulated news: Police to deploy face recognition cameras at all metro stations
events.body: Authorities cite safety and missing persons. Critics ask who stores the data and how long.

events.title: Simulated news: Gig delivery workers announce a citywide strike for a minimum hourly wage
events.body: Riders want a guaranteed wage and accident insurance. Platforms say costs will be passed to customers.

events.title: Simulated news: Neighbouring country's elected government suspended after army takes control 'to restore order'
events.body: The military promises elections 'when stability returns'. Some citizens welcome the end of chaos; others are protesting.

events.title: Simulated news: State extends free bus travel for women to all city routes
events.body: The government says ridership by working women has risen. The transport corporation's losses are growing.

events.title: Simulated news: Government to cut fuel and fertiliser subsidies by a third to reduce the deficit
events.body: Economists are split. Farmer groups threaten agitation; markets rally.

events.title: Simulated news: Internet shut down in parts of the old city for 48 hours after clashes
events.body: Officials say it stops rumours spreading. Shopkeepers and students say they lost work and classes.

events.title: Simulated news: Bill proposes rent control in metro cities, capping annual increases at 5%
events.body: Tenant groups welcome it. Landlords say they will take flats off the rental market.

events.title: Simulated news: Startup lays off 30% of staff, citing AI automation of support and testing roles
events.body: Former employees ask whether the state should tax automation or fund retraining.

events.title: Simulated news: European country votes to sharply limit immigration after months of protests
events.body: Supporters cite housing and jobs; opponents call it scapegoating of migrants.

events.title: Simulated news: Supreme Court hears petition to ban protests within 2 km of Parliament
events.body: Petitioners cite traffic and security. Opposition parties call it an attack on the right to protest.

events.title: Simulated news: State-run airline to be sold to a private conglomerate
events.body: The government says taxpayers can no longer fund losses. Employee unions want job guarantees.

events.title: Simulated news: Survey says most young urban Indians feel lonely despite being online all day
events.body: Researchers point to long commutes, migration for work and social media.

events.title: Simulated news: Proposal to make voting compulsory, with fines for not voting
events.body: Backers say it strengthens democracy; critics say forcing people to vote is itself undemocratic.

events.title: Simulated news: Government considers nationalising the country's largest cloud data centres for 'data sovereignty'
events.body: Foreign providers would have to sell local operations to a state company. Startups worry about prices and reliability.

events.title: Simulated news: Strongman president wins third term after changing term limits; crowds celebrate 'stability'
events.body: International observers question the vote. Supporters credit him with growth and order.
